stop_condition: Done when: (1) the round-9 delta is established against a real baseline rather than the specialist's report, and the claim 'the +1 is 1M.c7 alone, everything else comment-only' is confirmed or refuted mechanically; (2) the sentence-shape census is verified COMPLETE by a method that does not reuse the specialist's categories, and an eighth instance is either produced or its absence measured; (3) R8-F1's replacement census is checked reason-by-reason and site-by-site by MUTATION against the CURRENT file, with any new false reason named; (4) the 11-bare-plus-3-pinned=14 inventory is independently re-derived and the three-party disagreement settled; (5) the two unrequested fixes are ruled on for scope and accuracy; (6) the four-tier prediction 6107=5911+196 is checked against how the runner actually attributes a count. Then a finding at or above high, or verdict=approve.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/approval-record-disclosure-claim.test.sh:912, :928, :936 (the new R8-F1 census block at relpath_join)
findings.evidence: MEASURED against the shipped file, not read. All three occurrences of an assertion-total figure in this file are '195/0' (grep -nE '\b(18[0-9]|19[0-9]|20[0-9])\b' returns exactly :912 :928 :936), and the shipped file runs 196. Re-ran every mutation the prose describes, against the CURRENT file: (a) :912 'reversing any one alone leaves the suite at 195/0' — reversed each of the 8 order-insensitive sites individually (awk NR==N sub /| sort/ -> /| sort -r/ at :478 :498 :535 :562 :585 :589 :2544 :2547, mutation landed verified by diff of the single line): all 8 report '196 passed, 0 failed'. (b) :928 'pass 195/0 when all three are reversed TOGETHER' — reversing 470+823+827 together reports '196 passed, 0 failed'. (c) :936 'pinning any subset (e.g. QAG_SORTED/VBS_SORTED alone) still passes 195/0 TODAY' — pinning :823+:827 and leaving :470 bare reports '196 passed, 0 failed' under BOTH LC_ALL=C and LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8. So all three figures are stale by exactly the +1 this same round added, and were stale the moment they were written: the predecessor measured them correctly against a 195-assertion file and the same commit that transcribed them into prose added the 196th assertion.
findings.description: LOW, and not blocking. The load-bearing half of each figure is the '/0' — no assertion fails — and that is correct in all three cases; every conclusion the census draws from these mutations is independently confirmed above. Only the total is wrong, so a maintainer who re-runs the mutation sees '196 passed, 0 failed' and reaches the same conclusion the prose reaches. Recorded because it is the exact discipline of CONTRIBUTING.md's 'every number carries the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at', in the one file whose thesis is that documentation must be honest, and in the paragraph the dispatch brief asked me to check for mechanism-versus-stale-number discipline. The specialist caught this failure mode in its own draft for the naive-grep-count case and shipped it for the pass-count case three lines away. Cost to close: write '196/0' (or better, 'the suite still reports 0 failed'), which removes the coupling to the assertion total entirely.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/approval-record-disclosure-claim.test.sh:1373-1382 (1SM's '(4) EXECUTION' leg, one of the two UNREQUESTED fixes)
findings.evidence: The new head clause reads 'every assertion below exercises a REAL function this file already defines' and its own parenthetical immediately reads '(1SM.0 is `cat` over the seeded file; 1SM.1 calls discover_script_mirrors; 1SM.2 onward calls discover_operator_facing_surface / banned_claim_count ...)'. `cat` is not a function this file defines, so the head clause is false for 1SM.0 and the parenthetical states the counterexample in the same sentence. I VERIFIED every per-assertion fact in the parenthetical against the code and all are accurate: 1SM.0 is assert_contains over $(cat "$SCOPE_SANDBOX/HANDOFF.md") (:1390-1391); 1SM.1 calls discover_script_mirrors twice in a loop (:1405); 1SM.2 calls discover_operator_facing_surface (:1411); 1SM.3 calls banned_claim_count (:1418); 1SM.4 calls both (:1427-1431). So the facts are right and only the summarising clause overreaches. The sibling unrequested fix, 1S.13's EXECUTION leg (:1312-1320), is by contrast CORRECT and carefully scoped: 1S.13.1/.2/.3 do each run the extracted function as its own bash process (:1345 :1349 :1353 all `bash "$RELPATH_JOIN_{MUTANT,SHIPPED}"`), 0d is a real locale probe that does not (:1340-1341), and the claim 'none of it is a static grep of THIS FILE'S SOURCE' survives 0a/0b's greps because those grep the EXTRACTED file in $WORK, not this file.
findings.description: LOW, not blocking: nothing is unscanned or untested, 1SM.0's role is explicitly leg 1 (non-vacuity on the fixture) rather than exercising the scanner, and a reader gets the correct facts from the parenthetical. RULING ON THE BRIEF'S QUESTION, which the specialist asked openly. Both unrequested fixes were IN SCOPE to make: each corrected a demonstrably false claim in a file already open, found by the same sweep and the same method, and leaving a known-false claim in place would have been a deliberate choice to ship one. The shape distinction the specialist drew is also correct — these are methodology-execution claims, not coverage-of-scanning claims, so they are NOT the eighth instance of the seven-round series. But they DID warrant their own finding id, and the reason is now demonstrated rather than theoretical: folding them in meant they bypassed the finding-level scrutiny the four requested fixes received, and one of the two shipped a self-contradicting sentence that a finding-level pass would have caught. The general rule: an unrequested fix is welcome, and it earns an id precisely so someone reviews it against a stated criterion.

findings.location: LESSONS.md:257 (and :254) — OUTSIDE this change set, uncommitted working tree
findings.evidence: This is the count the brief asked me to settle, and it has been written into the durable ledger WRONG. LESSONS.md:257 states verbatim: 'Reported as "7 pinned / 12 bare / 19 total" sort sites when the truth was 2 real pinned invocations and 11 bare, 14 total'. Two errors: 2+11 is 13, not 14; and the pinned count is 3, not 2. MEASURED, by classifying every line in the shipped spec that pipes through sort (grep -nE '\bsort\b', 43 lines total, 26 of them comments): 11 BARE real invocations at :470 :478 :498 :535 :562 :585 :589 :823 :827 :2544 :2547, and 3 PINNED real invocations at :964 (relpath_join's own LC_ALL=C sort, load-bearing), :1340 (LC_ALL=C probe) and :1341 (LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 probe) — 14 real invocations. A further 3 non-comment lines (:1331 sed, :1334 and :1336 grep -c) carry the pin string as TEXT and execute no sort, which is exactly the trap that produced the original miscount. The spec file's own census prose states this correctly ('11 bare sort invocations + 3 locale-pinned ... = 14 real sort invocations total'), so the FILE is right and the LEDGER is wrong. Separately LESSONS.md:254 states the partition as '8 sites where order reaches no compared value, 3 where collation cancels by symmetry, and 2 whose consumer tests membership' over '11 bare sort sites' — which sums to 13.
findings.description: MEDIUM and deliberately NOT blocking: LESSONS.md is not in this change set (the gate reconcile subtracted it as already-baselined), approving pqnd does not ship it, and it carries no functional risk. It is recorded at MEDIUM rather than HIGH for that reason and because I cannot resolve it — CLAUDE.md forbids hand-editing the ledger, and lessons.sh dedups by normalised text, so a corrected re-add lands as a duplicate rather than a repair. WHY IT STILL MATTERS ENOUGH TO HEADLINE: the ledger is read by the orchestrator before decomposing non-trivial work and is fed to the grader as packet item 5, so this is the one artifact on the arc that outlives the task, and the entry carrying the wrong denominator is the entry whose subject is 'count call sites by what EXECUTES them, and state the denominator's provenance whenever a judgment rests on it'. The miscount's propagation path is now visible end to end: predecessor artifact prose -> dispatch brief -> LESSONS.md, with the specialist correcting it only in the file. ACTIONABLE WINDOW: LESSONS.md is uncommitted (git diff shows 17 added lines, none committed), so it can still be corrected in the working tree before commit without rewriting history. That window closes at the next commit. Suggested correction: ':257 -> 3 real pinned invocations and 11 bare, 14 total; four of the seven grep matches were prose about pinning'.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/approval-record-disclosure-claim.test.sh:911-924 (reason 1's '(8 sites)' annotation in the new census)
findings.evidence: The census frames itself as a partition — 'The 11 sites split into three genuinely different reasons' — then annotates reason 1 '(8 sites)' while handing two of those eight to reason 3 ('assert_names_defined/assert_names_invoked ... are covered by reason 3, below, not this one'), and reason 2 covers 3. Read off the annotations, 8+3+2 = 13 against a stated total of 11; read with the hand-off clause, the partition is 6+3+2 = 11, which is correct. The ambiguity is that '(8 sites)' counts the MEASURED reversal-pass set while the other two numbers count mechanism membership. I confirmed the reversal-pass set really is 8 (all 8 individual reversals report 196/0) and that reason 1's own mechanism text names exactly 6 of them (docs_md :478, operator_facing_surface :562, plugin_installed_files hook sub-list :535, QAG_COPIES/VBS_COPIES :585/:589, agents_md :498).
findings.description: LOW, and it is disambiguated in-line by a clause in the same bullet, so a reader who adds 8+3+2 has skipped a sentence telling them not to. Recorded anyway because the hazard is no longer theoretical: LESSONS.md:254 has ALREADY reproduced this exact framing as an 8/3/2 partition of 11 bare sites (see R9-F3), which is the annotation being read the way it invites. On a task where three separate parties have now miscounted this file's sort sites, a partition annotation whose arithmetic does not close against its own stated total is worth one more word. Cost to close: '(8 sites pass reversal individually; 6 of them for the reasons in this bullet, 2 under reason 3 below)'.
